newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers want transport fund off budget.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers want transport fund off budget.

text.p: A bipartisan majority in the House of Representatives co-sponsored a bill on Thursday to take transportation trust funds off-budget to make more money available for highways, aviation, harbors and waterways.

A similar bill passed the House last year by 284-143, but was never brought to a vote in the Senate. Supporters said its foes wanted to keep the money from the four trust funds in the general budget to help cut the overall budget deficit.
But Representative Bud Shuster, a leader in the off-budget effort, told a news conference he was "cautiously optimistic" that the bill would win Senate approval this year.
Shuster, chairman of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, said a similar bi-partisan "Truth in Budgeting Act" was likely to be introduced soon in the Senate.

The Pennsylvania Republican, said the bill, co-sponsored by 226 House members, would keep a promise that taxes levied on tranportation would be spent on transportation projects and not remain unspent in the general budget.

Republican aides said money now in the highway trust fund, obligated and unobligated, totaled $23.3 billion; in the aviation fund, $2.2 billion; in the inland waterway fund, $300 billion and in the harbor maintenance fund, $900 billion.

Shuster also said he would try to get the special 4.3 cents-a-gallon tax being assessed on unleaded gasoline to help reduce the budget deficit moved off-budget and allocated to highway and transit projects.
Aides said the move, to be attached to legislation to renew the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act, would provide $32 billion a year for highway projects and $6.5 billion for transit.
